title: Padding commutes with machine runs
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k$ work tapes, and let $K\ge k$. For every Boolean input word, every configuration $c$ of $M$ on that input, and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, running the machine padded to $K$ work tapes for $t$ steps from the padded configuration equals the padding to $K$ tapes of the $t$-step run of $M$ from $c$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
A natural number $K$ with $M$'s tape count $k\le K$
A configuration $c$ of $M$ on that input
replaced:
For every machine $M$, tape bound $K \ge k$, configuration $c$, and time $t$:
running the padded machine for $t$ steps from the padded configuration equals
padding the $t$-step run of $M$ from $c$ — the padded source observes exactly
its original work symbols.
